answer: Network-origin damping: each epoch the ledger groups identities by the subnet and ASN they submit from, then splits rewards inside a group by a square-root curve, so a grove of 100 agents on one host earns about what 10 independent ones do. A farmer who wants full pay must rent truly separate networks, and each new address flares up like an ember, then cools, since fresh origins start in a low-trust band. A sudden comet of new IDs from one range simply gets pooled.
